findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve AC3 'typed end-to-end' ownership: either fold the typed-transport deliverable into a roster child or amend the parent AC to reference cc77 as the covering (external) consumer.
evidence: Parent AC3: 'The reconciler transport is typed end-to-end, declared field asymmetries are pinned by property tests, and pagination loops are deduplicated into shared iterators.'
e931 Context: 'The typed-transport half of this hardening is already in flight as bug cc77 (in_progress) — do not duplicate it.'
e931 AC4: 'relates_to link recorded to cc77 (typed transport, separate in-flight work).' — a link, not delivery of the outcome.
cc77-8120 does not appear in the sibling roster; it is referenced only as external in-flight work.
findings.finding: Parent AC3 requires the reconciler transport be 'typed end-to-end', but child e931 — the only reconciler child in the roster — explicitly disclaims the typed-transport half ('The typed-transport half of this hardening is already in flight as bug cc77 ... do not duplicate it'; AC only records a relates_to link to cc77). cc77 is NOT a sibling in this epic's roster, so no child delivers the 'typed end-to-end' observable.
scenarios: Epic-close completion verifier checks whether every parent AC is delivered by a child; the 'typed end-to-end' clause of AC3 maps to no child deliverable in the subtree.
findings.suggested_fix: Amend parent AC3 to name cc77 as the consumer that delivers 'typed end-to-end' (covered-by-definition), or narrow AC3 to the property-test + pagination scope that e931 actually delivers and track typed-transport separately.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin the d37e-after-e602 landing order (or specify a temporary allowlist entry for reconcile-bridge.yml that e602 removes) so d37e's 'tree clean at landing' AC is satisfiable.
evidence: d37e AC: 'Tree is clean at landing (all existing bypasses routed or allowlisted with justification)' and 'CI fails on any raw git write against the store ... across Python, shell, and workflow YAML.'
reconcile-bridge.yml:290-291: 'git add -A' then 'git commit -m "chore: sync events from rebar reconciler ..."' inside .tickets-tracker.
e602 AC: 'The reconcile-bridge raw git write is routed through the canonical seam'; e602 description: 'companion: raw-git-write lint child, which this unblocks for .github'.
d37e and e602 carry mutual relates_to links but neither AC states a required landing order.
findings.finding: Ordering dependency without an ordering constraint: d37e's AC 'Tree is clean at landing' requires .github/workflows to contain no un-allowlisted raw git writes against the store, but reconcile-bridge.yml still runs a raw 'git add -A' / 'git commit' against the tickets tracker (lines ~290-291). e602 is the child that routes that write through the canonical seam. If d37e lands before e602, d37e's full-tree scan fails on reconcile-bridge.yml. The two are relates_to linked but no landing order is pinned.
scenarios: d37e lands first (or concurrently): its clean-tree gate flags reconcile-bridge.yml's raw git add/commit, blocking d37e's own landing or forcing a temporary allowlist entry that e602 must later remove.
findings.suggested_fix: State in d37e that it lands after e602 (or upgrade the relates_to to a blocks/depends edge), and note reconcile-bridge.yml as the specific site e602 must route first.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile 4b54 with the parent: add an acceptance criterion for the epic-close bug gate, or confirm 4b54 belongs under this epic.
evidence: Parent AC2 lists exactly six DET gate targets; an epic-close caused_by bug gate is not among them.
No parent AC references epic-close bug adjudication, caused_by floor, or a relevance screen.
4b54 is a full story (DET floor + candidate filter + haiku screen + verifier adjudication + sidecar tally) with its own regression backtest, i.e. non-trivial scope.
findings.finding: Parent/child scope inconsistency: child 4b54 (Epic-close bug gate: DET caused_by floor + haiku relevance screen + verifier adjudication) is a substantial deterministic close gate that no parent AC names. AC2 enumerates the DET pre-LLM gates the epic promises (raw git, unread config, wall-clock, unchecked AC, comment rot, oversized bug diff) and does not include an epic-close caused_by bug gate; no other parent AC covers it either.
scenarios: Epic completion review reconciles children to parent ACs; 4b54 delivers scope the parent never declared, so it is neither validated against nor traceable to any acceptance criterion.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a parent AC such as 'Epic close is gated on undispositioned caused-by/deliverable-defect bugs (DET floor + adjudicated relevance screen)' so 4b54 has a traceable parent criterion.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the concrete 'oversized' threshold (e.g. changed-lines/files count) used by both the pre-LLM gate (AC-2) and the Gerrit backstop (AC-8).
evidence: AC-2: 'oversized bug-fix diffs lacking a current plan-review attestation'
AC-8: 'the Gerrit backstop blocks oversized bug fixes lacking one'
'oversized' is an unbounded scope boundary (E2 signal 1) and the gate cannot be evaluated deterministically without a stated number/unit (F1)
findings.finding: The size threshold for 'oversized' bug-fix diffs is never stated, yet two gates (the pre-LLM gate in AC-2 and the Gerrit backstop in AC-8) must draw a concrete line to fire deterministically.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — AC-2 ('oversized bug-fix diffs lacking a current plan-review attestation') and AC-8 ('the Gerrit backstop blocks oversized bug fixes lacking one')
scenarios: Gate author must invent a diff-size cutoff; a reviewer cannot tell whether a given diff should have tripped the gate
findings.suggested_fix: Add a definition such as 'oversized = net diff > N changed lines across the fix commit(s)' and reference it from both AC-2 and AC-8.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Assign the rebar-debug/SKILL.md Phase-1-exit fix-plan hook to one owning child (78f1 or ad0d) and reflect it in that child's scope/AC.
evidence: ad0d Scope: 'rebar-debug skill Phase-1-exit hook: fix-plan-to-description + review-plan for non-trivial fixes (coordinate with the debug-skill child)'.

78f1 Scope: 'examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md (+ symlinked copy consistency; ~35-45 lines total)'; 78f1 ACs cover writebacks, Step-7 sweep, residual-risk, no-AGENTS.md — none mention a review-plan / fix-plan-to-description hook.
ad0d and 78f1 are mutually relates_to linked, but 78f1's authored SKILL.md content set omits the ad0d hook.
findings.finding: Scope overlap on the rebar-debug skill file: ad0d's scope adds a 'rebar-debug skill Phase-1-exit hook: fix-plan-to-description + review-plan for non-trivial fixes' to examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md — the same file 78f1 owns and rewrites (writebacks, two-axis Step-7 sweep, residual-risk). 78f1's scope and ACs do not mention or reserve room for ad0d's fix-plan hook, so the receiving child's coverage does not include the incoming block.
scenarios: Both children edit rebar-debug/SKILL.md; the second to land must merge the fix-plan hook into 78f1's rewritten Phase-1-exit section, and 78f1's completion (a specific ~35-45 line rewrite) may not have reserved the anchor for it.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the ad0d Phase-1-exit fix-plan-to-description hook into 78f1's SKILL.md scope (adding an AC line for it), leaving ad0d to own only the claimability/Gerrit-criterion code changes.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify a staged rollout (warn-then-enforce) and an explicit override/disable path for each new blocking DET gate and the Gerrit backstop, so a false positive does not hard-block all bug-fix commits.
evidence: AC line: 'Deterministic pre-LLM gates exist for: raw git writes bypassing the store seam, ... and oversized bug-fix diffs lacking a current plan-review attestation.'
AC line: 'the Gerrit backstop blocks oversized bug fixes lacking one'
ABSENCE: no epic-level statement of warn-mode/staged enablement, per-gate flags, or an override mechanism for false positives, nor a rollback path if a gate proves too aggressive.
findings.finding: The plan introduces multiple new blocking enforcement gates (DET pre-LLM gates that block code review, a Gerrit backstop that blocks oversized bug fixes, CI guards that fail on comment rot / raw-git-writes / unread config fields) but does not specify a staged rollout (warn-then-enforce) or an override/rollback path for when a gate misfires. A false-positive in any DET gate would block all legitimate bug-fix commits at 100% with no cheap escape hatch.
findings.location: AC: 'Deterministic pre-LLM gates exist for...' and 'the Gerrit backstop blocks oversized bug fixes lacking one'
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC that each new blocking gate ships first in advisory/warn mode with a documented per-gate enable flag and a bypass/override token, and that the Gerrit backstop has a cheap disable path.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Fix the e602/4527 ordering and target-form for the canary filer: decide whether the dedup pattern lands in the migrated Python (e602) or the YAML (4527), and sequence them.
evidence: e602 file_impact includes '.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge-canary.yml' (reason: 'canary logic migration').

4527 Scope: 'canary/heartbeat/binding-drift filer scripts or workflow logic (coordinate with Tier-3 migration child if concurrent)'; 4527 file_impact includes '.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge-canary.yml'.
e602 description/AC make no mention of 4527's dedup-pattern retrofit on the same canary filer.
findings.finding: Scope overlap: children e602 and 4527 both modify the canary filer workflow (.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge-canary.yml). e602 migrates canary run-block logic to Python; 4527 retrofits the dedup/threshold/template pattern into the same canary filer. Only 4527 flags the coordination ('coordinate with Tier-3 migration child if concurrent'); e602 does not acknowledge 4527, and neither AC set fixes a merge order for the shared file.
scenarios: Whichever lands second rewrites/relocates the canary filer body the first authored (Python entry point vs. dedup-in-YAML), risking a lost-update or double-migration of the same filer.
findings.suggested_fix: Sequence e602 before 4527 and have 4527 apply the dedup+threshold+template pattern to the migrated Python filer, so there is a single canary-filer implementation.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Clarify that AC-2 (local pre-LLM gate) and AC-8 (server-side Gerrit backstop) are intentionally distinct layers, or merge them if they are the same requirement.
evidence: AC-2: '...oversized bug-fix diffs lacking a current plan-review attestation.'
AC-8: '...the Gerrit backstop blocks oversized bug fixes lacking one.'
Both block the same event (oversized bug fix without plan review) at different points
findings.finding: AC-2 (pre-LLM gate blocking oversized bug fixes lacking plan-review attestation) and AC-8 (Gerrit backstop blocking oversized bug fixes lacking a review) describe near-duplicate enforcement without stating how the two layers differ or relate.
scenarios: A reader/implementer cannot tell whether these are one gate described twice or two intentional layers (local pre-LLM check vs server-side Gerrit backstop)
findings.suggested_fix: State e.g. 'AC-2 is the local pre-LLM advisory gate; AC-8 is the non-bypassable Gerrit-side backstop enforcing the same contract at submit time.'

findings.finding: Several gates encode thresholds ('oversized bug-fix diffs', 'DET caused_by floor') that are the kind of rule expected to be tuned as false-positive rates surface, but the epic does not state at any altitude that these thresholds are configurable rather than hardcoded.
